name_en: Tobitsuki dango — mochi dumplings coated in sweetened cowpea beans
summary_ja: もち米にうるち米を混ぜた生地を茹で、砂糖水に浸したササゲをまぶすあわら市周辺のお盆の菓子。薄赤い豆が餅に飛びついたように見えることが名前の由来とされ、控えめな甘さの素朴な味と伝わる。
summary_en: A dough of glutinous and non-glutinous rice flour is boiled and coated with cowpea beans soaked in sugar water — an Obon sweet from around Awara city. The name is said to come from the pale red beans looking as if they had 'jumped onto' the mochi, its sweetness kept modest.
source_title: とびつき団子 福井県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Decchi yokan — a thin, watery winter yokan cut from a shallow tray
summary_ja: こしあんに寒天と砂糖、塩を溶かして固める、水羊かんに近い福井の冬の菓子。京都へ丁稚奉公に出た若者が正月に持ち帰った羊かんを水で伸ばして配ったのが始まりと伝わり、こたつで食べるのが定番という。
summary_en: Sweet red bean paste is set with agar, sugar, and a pinch of salt into a thin, water-yokan-like winter confection. It is said to have begun when a young apprentice, home for New Year from a Kyoto shop, stretched a bar of yokan with water to share with neighbors, eaten by the kotatsu.
source_title: でっち羊かん 福井県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kashiwa mochi — a rice cake filled with sweet bean paste, wrapped in oak leaf
summary_ja: 米粉の生地を蒸してつき、あんを包んでかしわの葉で包む小浜市・若狭町の田植え祝いの菓子。5月半ばから7月にかけて集落ごとの「田の神祭り」で神輿を担ぐ日に用意され、親類にも配ると伝わる。
summary_en: Rice-flour dough is steamed, pounded, wrapped around sweet bean paste, and folded in an oak leaf — a rice-planting celebration sweet from Obama and Wakasa town. It is prepared for each community's 'god of the rice paddy' festival between mid-May and July, and shared with relatives.
source_title: 柏餅 福井県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
